title: Why Startups Should Use Fractional Recruiting (October 2026)
summary: Fractional recruiting fits startup hiring that comes in waves. See five reasons: variable capacity, role-specific expertise, and cost control in 2026.
body_markdown:
[Startup hiring](https://www.dover.com/) rarely arrives at a steady, predictable pace. You might need to fill five engineering roles in six weeks after closing a round, then pause hiring entirely while the product catches up. That mismatch between variable demand and fixed recruiting capacity is the structural problem the fractional model was built to solve, and it’s why some early-stage teams treat recruiting as a function to dial up or down, not a headcount to carry year-round.


**TLDR:**


-


Startup recruiting demand often follows growth plans, with sharp spikes and pauses that can strain fixed recruiting capacity.


-


Fractional recruiting lets you match specialists to each role type instead of relying on one generalist for every hire.


-


Blending senior recruiters at 5-10 hours per week for strategy with junior recruiters handling sourcing and coordination can cut costs when their rates and hours fit the workload.


-


Fractional arrangements can let you ramp up after a funding round and scale back during product development without adding permanent headcount, depending on recruiter availability and engagement terms.


-


Some fractional recruiter marketplaces give early-stage startups access to experienced recruiters on a per-engagement basis.


## How the Fractional Model Fits Recruiting


Fractional work gives companies access to experienced specialists for part of their week.[The 2026 Fractional Work Report](https://www.fractionaljobs.io/the-fractional-work-report) describes professionals who often serve multiple clients and perform hands-on work alongside advisory tasks. Its findings cover fractional work across functions, not recruiting alone, so they do not prove recruiting-specific growth or hiring outcomes. For a startup, the practical question is whether a recruiter’s available hours and expertise fit the searches at hand.


Without a shared pipeline, a fractional recruiter’s sourcing notes end up in a personal spreadsheet or inbox, and a hiring manager can message a candidate the recruiter already contacted. An ATS handles the tracking and stage data; the recruiter supplies sourcing and screening hours on top of it. Some tools, including Dover, pair a free ATS with on-demand fractional recruiter access, so internal teams and recruiters can work from the same candidate records. Startups can run searches themselves or add recruiting support without moving their pipeline to a separate system.


Model Cost Structure Flexibility Best For


Fractional Recruiter Hourly, retainer, or per-hire fee; contract length varies by agreement Can scale up or down, subject to recruiter availability and engagement terms Startups with variable or stage-driven hiring needs


Full-Time In-House Recruiter Fixed salary plus benefits Low: headcount stays constant regardless of hiring volume Companies with steady, high-volume hiring pipelines


Contingency Agency Percentage of first-year salary (typically[15-25% contingency fee rates](https://www.leonar.app/blog/how-much-do-recruitment-agencies-charge/) ) Medium: engage per role, but fees are high per hire One-off or urgent roles where speed outweighs cost


## 1. Hire Specialized Recruiters for Every Role


**Why it matters** : Your startup needs different types of talent at different stages.


Using[fractional recruiting](https://www.dover.com/blog/fractional-recruiting-employers-guide) allows you to tap into specialized recruiters to hire for specific roles:


-


Engineering recruiters for your technical roles


-


Sales recruiters for your go-to-market hires


-


Executive recruiters for your leadership positions


Compared with relying on a single full-time generalist recruiter, this specialization can provide relevant expertise when a search requires role-specific knowledge.


## 2. Scale Resources With Changing Hiring Demands


**Why it matters** : Startup hiring often comes in waves, not steady streams. For example, you might hire a lot after a fundraising round, and then pause hiring for the next 6 months.


The fractional model allows you to:


-


Ramp up after funding rounds, subject to recruiter availability


-


Scale back during your product development phases


-


Adjust recruiting hours as market conditions change, within agreed engagement terms


This flexibility can reduce the risk of[in-house recruiters](https://www.dover.com/blog/fractional-recruiter-vs-full-time-recruiter-which-is-right-for-your-startup) being overworked or underutilized when hiring demand changes. Sharing a pipeline can make the ramp-up/ramp-down cycle easier to manage. A shared ATS keeps sourcing activity, candidate history, and stage data visible to team members with access, which can reduce coordination work and duplicate outreach when records stay current and handoff responsibilities are clear.


## 3. Access Top-Tier Recruiting Talent


**Why it matters** : Early-stage startups need elite recruiting strategy but often can’t afford full-time top-tier recruiter salaries. Fractional recruiting carries a different cost structure from agency placement fees, which scale with the candidate’s salary.


Fractional recruiting provides:


-


Insights into candidate messaging from recruiters working across multiple startups


-


Strategic guidance suited to your startup’s stage and hiring needs


-


Engagement that can be cost-effective when the workload fits limited senior recruiter hours (e.g., 5-10 hours/week)


## 4. Delegate Day-to-Day Recruiting


**Why it matters** : Recruiting involves both high-level strategy and day-to-day operations. When you hire a full-time recruiter, they must do low-level administrative work too.


The fractional model allows you to hire:


-


Senior recruiters (5-10 hours/week) focusing on strategy and accountability


-


Junior recruiters (20-30 hours/week) handling sourcing, coordination, and candidate experience


This blended approach can be effective for recruiting when strategic and day-to-day tasks have clear owners, and can save you money when recruiter rates, hours, and coordination costs fit the workload.


## 5. Accelerate Feedback Loops and Pivot Quickly


**Why it matters** : In your fast-paced startup world, quick adjustments are important.


With agreed review checkpoints and room to adjust recruiter hours, fractional recruiting can offer:


-


Faster evaluation of recruiter performance


-


Easy pivoting if strategies aren’t working


-


Rapid scaling of successful approaches


This agility is especially valuable in recruiting, where outcomes can heavily impact your overall company direction.


## October 2026: AI Screening Responsibilities Across Recruiter Handoffs


A recruiter leaving a search can leave behind AI screening scores without a clear record of how they influenced candidate decisions. For teams planning their next hiring cycle in October 2026, that is a practical gap worth checking.[Kilpatrick’s June 2026 Illinois AI notice update](https://ktslaw.com/insights/alert/2026/6/illinois-department-of-human-rights-issues-proposed-rules-on-ai-notice-requirements-in-employment-decisions) reports that the Illinois Department of Human Rights temporarily withdrew its proposed implementing rules to allow more collaboration with other state agencies. The statutory obligations for AI use in employment decisions, effective January 1, 2026, remain in effect during the withdrawal.


In a fractional engagement, the scope of work can specify which screening tools are permitted, who reviews their recommendations, and where decision records stay when the engagement ends. For example, a handoff note could record the screening tool and version, the role’s scoring criteria, the screening date, and the human reviewer’s decision with its rationale, including any override of the AI recommendation. The outgoing recruiter can flag candidates still awaiting human review and name the incoming owner, who confirms access to those records before taking over. A shared ATS can support that handoff, but software access alone does not settle legal responsibilities. Applicable notice and recordkeeping duties need review with counsel based on where hiring takes place.

The right model depends on your stage and hiring volume, but the structural argument for fractional recruiting gets stronger the more variable your hiring needs are. ## FAQs


### Do I need an ATS before bringing in a fractional recruiter?


An ATS records candidates and stages but does not source, screen, or persuade anyone. A fractional recruiter supplies those hours and judgment but needs a place to keep the work. A startup does not strictly need a new ATS first, since many recruiters can work in a client’s existing tools, including a spreadsheet. A shared ATS tends to be the cleaner path because the recruiter and the hiring team see the same candidate history, which can reduce duplicate outreach. One option is a free ATS paired with an on-demand recruiter marketplace, such as Dover’s, so both sit in one system.


### What is the difference between an ATS and full recruiting support?


An ATS organizes a pipeline, but it does not find candidates or close them. Full recruiting support adds the people doing that work: sourcing, screening, scheduling, and offer negotiation. Teams with a few straightforward roles can often run an ATS on their own. When a role is senior or specialized, or no one on the team has recruiting bandwidth, a fractional recruiter can plug in on top of the ATS for the hours a search needs.


### What tools do fractional recruiters use?


Most work across four categories: sourcing tools for finding and contacting candidates, an ATS for tracking stages, calendar tools for scheduling, and email for outreach. Many fractional recruiters adapt to the client’s ATS instead of requiring a new one. Keeping the candidate data, sourcing notes, and outreach history in the client’s own ATS means each new search can build on earlier work instead of starting from zero.


### How do you keep candidate history intact when a recruiter hands off a search?


Handoff gaps usually appear when screening scores, sourcing notes, and stage data live in the outgoing recruiter’s own files. Storing them in a shared ATS keeps them visible to the hiring team and the incoming recruiter. Clear handoff responsibilities matter as much as the software: the outgoing recruiter can flag candidates awaiting review, and the incoming recruiter can confirm access to those records before taking over.


### How does fractional recruiter pricing compare with a contingency agency?


A fractional engagement’s cost does not scale with the candidate’s salary, while a contingency fee does. Contingency fees commonly run 15% to 25% of first-year salary, which can mean $24,000 to $40,000 on a $160,000 hire. Dover’s marketplace averages about $4,800 per hire across all roles, and the figure varies by role complexity, seniority, and recruiter.


## Final Thoughts on Fractional Recruiting


The five reasons in this post are all expressions of the same underlying reality:[startup hiring](https://www.dover.com/) is too uneven, too role-specific, and too consequential to treat as a fixed cost. Fractional recruiting fits that reality not because it is a cheaper version of something else, but because it is a different structural model, one where expertise, capacity, and cost all move with your actual hiring needs instead of ahead of them. Whether you are building your first recruiting motion after a seed round or trying to scale a pipeline without adding permanent headcount, the question worth asking is whether your current approach is built for the hiring cadence you actually have, not the one you wish you had.
